## Declarations and implementations

```plato
//==
// # Keyframes
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Animation blending
//  - Animation clips and playback
//  - Keyframes and tracks

//==
// # Animation blending
//
// The structures that combine several clips into one result: weighted, possibly
// additive layers in a blend stack, and the one- and two-dimensional blend
// spaces that mix clips by a continuous parameter.

// One clip's contribution in a blend stack. Weight scales the clip's influence;
// when IAdditive is true the clip's values are added on top of the layers below
// instead of interpolated with them.
type AnimationLayer
{
    Clip: AnimationClip;
    Weight: Proportion;
    Additive: Boolean;
}

// A clip placed at a position along a one-dimensional blend axis.
type BlendSpaceSample1D
{
    Position: Number;
    Clip: AnimationClip;
}

// Blends clips by a single parameter (walk speed, aim angle): sampling at a
// parameter value interpolates the clips nearest it. Samples are ordered by
// ascending Position.
type BlendSpace1D
{
    Samples: Array<BlendSpaceSample1D>;
}

// A clip placed at a position on a two-dimensional blend plane.
type BlendSpaceSample2D
{
    Position: Number2;
    Clip: AnimationClip;
}

// Blends clips by two parameters (strafe and forward speed): sampling at a
// point interpolates the surrounding clips.
type BlendSpace2D
{
    Samples: Array<BlendSpaceSample2D>;
}

//==
// # Animation clips and playback
//
// Self-contained bundles of named tracks, the trigger events on their time
// lines, the playhead that runs them, and the finite state machine that
// sequences one clip into the next. Event times are Duration offsets from the
// start of the owning clip.

// A named trigger on a clip's time line, with an opaque payload for the
// consumer. Time is the offset from the start of the clip.
type AnimationEvent
{
    Time: Duration;
    Name: String;
    Payload: String;
}

// A named, self-contained bundle of animation: typed named tracks, trigger
// events, and a total Duration. Track names address targets in the consumer;
// tracks whose keys extend past Duration are clipped by the player.
type AnimationClip
{
    Name: String;
    Duration: Duration;
    Events: Array<AnimationEvent>;
    NumberTracks: Array<NamedTrack<Number>>;
    Vector2DTracks: Array<NamedTrack<Vector2D>>;
    Vector3DTracks: Array<NamedTrack<Vector3D>>;
    QuaternionTracks: Array<NamedTrack<Quaternion>>;
    ColorTracks: Array<NamedTrack<Color>>;
    TransformTracks: Array<NamedTrack<TrsTransform3D>>;
}

// The direction time advances during playback.
type PlaybackDirection = Forward | Reverse;

// The playback position and rate of a running animation. Time is the offset
// into the clip; Speed is a rate multiplier (1 is natural speed).
type AnimationPlayhead
{
    Time: Duration;
    Speed: Number;
    Direction: PlaybackDirection;
    Playing: Boolean;
}

// A zero-based index of a state within an animation state machine's States
// array. -1 means "any state" where a transition allows it.
type AnimationStateIndex
    implements IValue, IHashable, IComparable, IIndex
{
    Value: Integer;
}

// A named node in an animation state machine: the clip it plays, its rate
// multiplier, and whether it loops while active.
type AnimationState
{
    Name: String;
    Clip: AnimationClip;
    Speed: Number;
    Looping: Boolean;
}

// A directed edge between states. FromState and ToState index the owning
// machine's States; FromState -1 means "from any state". ExitTime is the
// normalized time in the source state at which the transition may fire (0
// means immediately); Duration is the cross-fade length shaped by Easing.
type AnimationTransition
{
    FromState: AnimationStateIndex;
    ToState: AnimationStateIndex;
    Duration: Duration;
    Easing: ClassicEasing;
    ExitTime: Proportion;
}

// A finite state machine over animation states. InitialState indexes States.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finite-state_machine)
type AnimationStateMachine
{
    States: Array<AnimationState>;
    Transitions: Array<AnimationTransition>;
    InitialState: AnimationStateIndex;
}

//==
// # Keyframes and tracks
//
// Typed keys on a time line and the tracks that interpolate between them: the
// interpolation and extrapolation policies, plain and tangent-handled keys,
// single-value and named tracks, and the per-channel transform tracks. Key
// times are Duration offsets from the start of the owning track.

// How a track interpolates between a key and its successor: hold the key's
// value until the next key (Constant), interpolate linearly, follow a smooth
// spline with automatic tangents (CubicSpline), use explicit weighted tangent
// handles (Bezier) or explicit tangent slopes (Hermite), or approach the next
// value like a damped spring (Spring).
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interpolation)
type KeyInterpolation = Constant | Linear | CubicSpline | Bezier | Hermite | Spring;
```
